jobs.description: Our operations network, known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service, delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. To keep our operations network secure and assure operational continuity, we are looking for a hands-on and detail-oriented professional who wants to join our team as Security and Loss Prevention (SLP) Specialist. In this key role, you will be responsible for the day-to-day execution of security operations, delivering concrete on-the-ground contributions through direct operational support to our sites. You will deliver security as a service to our operational sites across the end-to-end supply chain to protect our people and prevent loss. Key job responsibilities • Execute day-to-day security operations and conduct regular physical security checks at assigned sites • Support resilience of our business operations by contributing to emergency and crisis planning for sites within your area of responsibility • Contribute to the identification of vulnerabilities (e.g., loss, associate experience, process improvement) and define appropriate mitigating actions while ensuring compliance with legal and ethical standards • Serve as point of contact for and coordinate measures to manage risk with local management and external parties (e.g., law enforcement agencies and industry associations) on all security-related matters • Ensure compliance of your assigned sites with Amazon global security standards A day in the life As an SLP Specialist, you will join a team of Security and Loss Prevention professionals providing security as a service to business customers across multiple business units within a dedicated geographical area. Your daily focus will be on hands-on execution of security operations, including conducting physical security rounds, monitoring CCTV systems, and responding to immediate security concerns. You perform regular physical security audits and investigate policy violations, security-related incidents, and loss events. During your investigations, you collect information by monitoring systems and tools, analysing data reports, and conducting interviews. You execute established procedures to address security incidents and implement approved solutions for identified vulnerabilities. Your findings help to identify vulnerabilities in our processes, for which you contribute to the development of mitigating measures. You play a key role in maintaining the physical integrity of our sites by auditing and monitoring the health status of our systems and, jointly with subject matter experts and external suppliers, maintain their functionality. You interact on a daily basis with our external security service providers to ensure delivery of high-quality security services and a smooth customer experience. You also act as point of contact for multiple internal and external departments (e.g., legal, HR, security service providers, local law enforcement) and subject matter expert in Security and Loss Prevention-related matters. Finally, you deliver loss prevention-related education and awareness programs to other teams and liaise with various stakeholders on policy and procedure across all management levels. About the team Sitting within the Worldwide Operations Security organisation, Security and Loss Prevention supports the accomplishment of Amazon´s business targets and the strengthening of our brand by effectively protecting against relevant threats and by managing security and loss prevention risks that could: • Put our associates and customers under jeopardy • Disrupt the continuity of our business operations • Inflict damage to our assets • Have adverse impact on our brand reputation Working in partnership with our stakeholders, we secure the Amazon supply chain end-to-end and promote security during business conversations. We do this by preventing security and loss prevention-related risks and vulnerabilities as early as possible, intervening in unfolding incidents to minimize any negative impact as well as thoroughly investigating security-related incidents to identify and remove root causes, preventing reoccurrence.

Scopely is looking for a
Director of Quality Assurance
to join the development team for our new free-to-play Adventure Game, bringing an iconic and beloved IP to players around the world on mobile and PC. This role can be based in our Culver City hub or remotely within the US or Canada.
At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day — whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing, and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.
What You Will Do
As the
Director of Quality Assurance
, you will shape and drive the quality vision for one of Scopely’s most ambitious upcoming projects. You will be accountable for defining and executing QA strategies that ensure every player experiences a consistently high-quality, globally resonant game while empowering a growing development team to deliver on our aspirations.
This is both a strategic and operational leadership role with a strong technical focus. We intend to heavily leverage automation to deliver high-quality experiences and interactions at scale. As the project evolves, you will build and lead a team of quality professionals across multiple initiatives and regions, while developing modern tools, automation, and processes.
You will partner closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to champion a culture of quality throughout the organization. You will also play an instrumental role in shaping how the team iterates toward success and continuously evolves its ways of working.
Craft & Technical Excellence
Drive the adoption of modern testing strategies, automation frameworks, and tooling to support multi-platform development across PC and mobile, internal and external development teams, and generated content.
Apply deep technical expertise to develop and leverage test automation that enables rapid development while maintaining a high bar for quality.
Establish, monitor, and evolve KPIs and quality metrics that assess product health, identify risks, and guide continuous improvement.
Partner with development teams to embed quality practices throughout the development lifecycle rather than relying solely on end-stage testing.
Continuously evaluate opportunities to improve QA efficiency, coverage, scalability, and reliability through automation and tooling.
Strategic & Organizational Leadership
Define and execute a scalable, long-term QA vision and roadmap aligned with the project’s product and operational strategies.
Own the QA organizational structure, hiring strategy, and resourcing plans in alignment with the project vision, budget, and team growth needs.
Influence product leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to embed quality considerations throughout the product lifecycle.
Build a culture of ownership, accountability, innovation, and bias toward action within the QA discipline.
Develop a deep understanding of the product, its IP, and its core gameplay systems to effectively support ongoing quality efforts and evolving project needs.
Partner with senior leadership to identify quality risks, establish priorities, and ensure QA strategy evolves alongside the project.
People & Talent Development
Exemplify Scopely’s core tenets and serve as a role model across the team.
Foster an inclusive and engaging team culture where Scopeleans can do their best work.
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing QA organization across multiple initiatives and locations.
Identify and address capability gaps across the QA team, proactively developing future-ready talent and leadership pipelines.
What We’re Looking For
Significant experience leading Quality Assurance within game development, including experience operating at a senior leadership level.
Strong technical expertise and a proven ability to achieve high levels of quality through automated testing across multiple phases of game development.
Experience designing, implementing, or scaling test automation frameworks and modern QA tooling.
Demonstrated experience supporting complex, multi-platform products, ideally across PC and mobile.
Exceptional leadership and people management skills, with a track record of building, developing, and leading high-performing teams.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with excellent attention to detail.
Strong organizational, prioritization, time management, and accountability skills.
Strong negotiation and influencing skills, with the ability to advocate effectively for your team while balancing broader product and business priorities.
A proactive, enthusiastic, and self-motivated approach, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.
Comfortable working within an agile development environment and managing quality coverage across multiple high-profile releases with strict deadlines.
Exceptional reporting capabilities, including the ability to translate quality data and metrics into clear insights for senior stakeholders.
Extensive knowledge of Jira or comparable defect-tracking and development-management systems.
Willingness to travel occasionally to collaborate with teams across Scopely hub locations.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

jobs.description: Space-1 is NVIDIA's first Orbital Data Center (ODC) module — a Vera Rubin–class compute platform engineered for low-Earth orbit mission. It is the first step in a multi-generation orbital roadmap to speed up AI adoption. We are looking for a strong technical architect to own end-to-end system software architecture for Space-1 and successor orbital platforms. You will architect the full stack — application to libraries, from data center stack to BMC and BIOS firmware, manageability, and telemetry through the host OS, GPU and CPU drivers, and CUDA — to deliver a production-ready inference platform that operates reliably in the radiation, thermal-cycling, and remote-operations environment of LEO. You will partner closely with the orbital hardware system architecture team, drive customer use cases with constellation operators, align architecture with mission requirements, and bring the best orbital AI products to market. Join us at the forefront of technological advancement. What you'll be doing: Own system architecture for inference stack and other applications running on this class of products and make it resilient to any fault happening in space. Co-architect with the orbital hardware system architecture team to define interfaces, partitioning, and trade-offs across silicon, board, firmware, OS, and AI workload layers for 5-year LEO missions. Own end-to-end system software architecture for Space-1 and successor Orbital Data Center modules — covering data center stack, BMC firmware, BIOS, host OS, GPU/CPU drivers, CUDA, DCGM, and manageability telemetry as a single integrated stack. Define the manageability architecture for an unreachable, autonomous data center: remote bring-up, in-orbit firmware update, dual-module redundancy, fault containment, recovery from SEU/SEFI events, and telemetry for fleets ranging from tens to millions of nodes. Architect rad-tolerant system software behaviors — ECC handling, memory scrubbing, latch-up mitigation, deterministic recovery, and graceful degradation through 5 years and up to ~8,000 thermal cycles in dawn–dusk sun-synchronous orbit. Drive Redfish, MCTP, PLDM, and constellation-level management protocols across BMC, BIOS, and host software so customers can operate orbital fleets with the same tools they use on the ground. Define minimum BMC feature set, pin budget, boot architecture (rugged M.2 / VPX-class options), and dual-module redundancy strategy in partnership with platform and mechanical engineering. Partner with cloud and constellation customers (SpaceX, Blue Origin, Starcloud, Planet, Cowboy Space, and others) to translate mission requirements — orbit, duty cycle, NSA PHIPs security, post-quantum networking (CX9), inference SLAs — into actionable platform software architecture. Drive reliability and optimization in the system software architecture from an orbital data center viewpoint, including correct operation through eclipse periods and idle-power retention strategies. Work closely with the bring-up team and resolve issues at Speed of Light from first silicon through first launch. jobs.description:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit
www.bitgo.com
.
This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.
Why this role exists
BitGo's product is the foundation of the crypto industry globally. Our products and services are used by a breadth of client types worldwide: exchanges, banks, fintechs, asset managers, protocols, corporates, and governments. Much of the industry's infrastructure ultimately runs on or intersects with our platform. Delivery at that scale, across that many client types and jurisdictions, is executed by single-threaded PM owners. The individual workstreams are owned. What is not owned is the connective tissue between them: delivery operating rhythm, cross-team dependencies, regulatory submission pipelines, audit-driven remediation programs, etc that cut across product, engineering, compliance, legal, and finance.
You will join as the first program manager for R&D and build the Technical Program Management function from scratch within your first year. This is not a process-improvement role. It is an execution-risk role at a public company where missed delivery on regulated commitments has audit, examiner, and investor consequences.
What you will own
Timely and predictable delivery of product.
This is the mandate everything else serves. You own delivery integrity across the product portfolio: dates that mean something, cross-team and cross-entity programs (acquisition integrations, legal-entity restructurings, partner and vendor migrations) executed end-to-end, and early escalation the moment a plan and a commitment diverge. When BitGo says something ships, it ships.
Building trust between product and our regulatory, compliance, legal, finance, and audit partners.
Run the programs where product delivery and control exposure intersect: new-product regulatory review pipelines with fixed examiner deadlines, remediation of audit findings where the fix is a product build, and delivery against commitments made to regulators. These partner teams need to trust that product's plans are real and product needs to trust that review clocks are predictable; you are the person who makes both true, and who forces conflicts between remediation timelines and exposure windows into explicit decisions rather than letting them ride.
Portfolio dependency and capacity integrity.
Maintain the single source of truth for where resources are allocated, which programs must land when, and what is at risk. Surface contradictions, such as committed goals with unstaffed critical-path dependencies, duplicate ownership, or cross-team dependencies that live in nobody's plan, before they surface as quarter-end misses. Build a credible picture of keep-the-lights-on load so real capacity is known, not guessed.
Portfolio dependency and capacity integrity.
Maintain the single source of truth for where resources are allocated, which programs must land when, and what is at risk. Surface contradictions — committed goals with unstaffed critical-path dependencies, duplicate ownership, cross-team dependencies that live in nobody's plan — before they surface as quarter-end misses. Build a credible picture of keep-the-lights-on load so real capacity is known, not guessed.
The product operating rhythm.
Run the execution-review cadence for the product org: initiative status that is current and honest, launch readiness that commercial can sell against, and a working blocker-escalation path with SLAs. You make status cheap to produce and impossible to fudge.
The TPM team.
You start as the first program manager for R&D, hands-on, running the highest-exposure programs yourself, and build out the function within a year, hiring 1–2 TPMs against proven need. Set the bar for what program management means here: outcome-accountable, technically fluent, and light-touch on teams that are already delivering.
What success looks like in the first two quarters
Every regulated-delivery program has a dated plan reconciled against its external deadline, with gaps escalated in writing. There should be no compliance commitment tracked in a spreadsheet nobody owns.
Committed goals and staffing are reconciled: zero commitments with unstaffed critical-path dependencies that leadership hasn't explicitly accepted.
One integration or entity program demonstrably run end-to-end through your operating model.
Product leads report the coordination overhead went
down
, not up. If the org experiences TPM as a reporting tax, the function has failed regardless of the dashboards.
Who you will partner with
Product managers
, who keep outcome accountability and decide what to build. You take the cross-team coordination load off their plate and bring escalation muscle when a blocker sits in another org.
Engineering leadership
, who own technical decisions, estimates, and delivery. You provide program-level sequencing and a single dependency view across teams, operating by partnership rather than positional authority.
Compliance, legal, and risk
, who own regulatory judgment. You build the delivery machine around that judgment — submission pipelines, review-clock tracking, and remediation plans mapped to the audit calendar.
Commercial leadership
, who own revenue and client commitments. You give them launch dates they can sell against and a real intake path when deal-driven commitments need to enter the roadmap.
Finance and audit
, for whom you keep control-remediation milestones honest against the audit calendar, with slippage escalated the week it happens.
What we're looking for
8+ years in technical program management, with 3+ leading TPM teams or functions, ideally including founding one.
Delivery leadership in a
regulated financial environment
: you have run programs with examiner deadlines, audit findings, SOX-adjacent controls, or material-weakness remediation, and you know how public-company audit exposure changes program management.
Technically credible with platform engineering: you can read an architecture discussion, pressure-test an estimate, and hold your own on sequencing conversations with senior engineers without pretending to be one.
Demonstrated experience with at least one of: M&A integration, legal-entity restructuring, or large multi-party partner migrations.
Operates through influence in organizations where authority is split across reporting lines. You get things done with people who don't report to you and don't want another meeting.
Writing-first operator: your default artifacts are documents and dependency maps, not status meetings.
Crypto/digital-asset domain experience is a plus, not a requirement. Regulated-fintech delivery scar tissue matters more.
What will make you fail here
Treating this as a process-rollout role. The org is allergic to ceremony and the CEO is hands-on; value has to show up as
delivered programs
, fast.
Needing positional authority to operate. Engineering does not report into product; you will coordinate across that line daily.
Why Join BitGo?
Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world's financial markets.
Here are some of the benefits* of working at BitGo:
Competitive base salary, bonus and stock options
100% company paid health insurance for employee, partner and dependents
Up to 4% 401k company match
Paid parental leave, Paid vacation
Free custom lunches, dinners and snacks
Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs
Great colleagues and inspiring startup environment
Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you’ll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.
Pay Transparency Notice:
Depending upon your leveling the compensation for this role averages between $200,000 - $230,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus and the benefits outlined above are also a part of this role's package.
